CVE-2026-109619. Anything serving PHP is affected, whatever sits on top of it.

1. Update PHP. 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36, 8.2.35, or your distro's backport.
2. Restart PHP. A pool loads its binary once and serves from it until it
restarts, so the fix on disk reaches nothing already running.

PHP 8.1 is past end of life and gets no fix. Move those sites.

posts.content:
PSA: #php2shell gives attackers remote code execution on php servers pre-authentication, and @fastly.com has seen active attack activity.

Here is what you need to know:

* Two critical PHP vulnerabilities disclosed today (CVE-2026-109618, CVE-2026-109619, CVSS 9.2 

* The root is a decades-old design choice in PHP's error handling (described more in our post)

* There was evidence of in-the-wild exploitation pre-disclosure. 

The potential impact cannot be overstated:
* Breadth: Any organization with PHP applications
* Depth: The attacker can do what they want in the application

We can confirm we have seen attack activity on Fastly's network, including exploitation attempts pre-disclosure.

What to do right now:

The PHP Foundation released patches this morning; we encourage all organizations to patch immediately if they can.

Assume every maintained PHP version is affected. At this time, the oldest demonstrated exploit path has been present since 2012. 

The patches fix the demonstrated exploit paths; the underlying architecture remains vulnerable. Expect novel variants and a ramp-up in exploitation attempts over the next 24 to 48 hours. 

Fastly NGWAF customers should immediately apply the Virtual Patch for CVE-2026-109618 & CVE-2026-109619 to all services that may be vulnerable.

Our detection content looks for the structural hallmarks of these exploitation attempts that may indicate potential exploitation attempts of php2shell CVEs.

Reach out if Fastly can provide immediate help for you to stay safe: support@fastly.com

Learn more about what’s going on, what to do, what’s next here: https://www.fastly.com/blog/fastlys-proactive-protection-critical-php-rce-cve-2026-109618

PHP InfoSec

Wise system administrators who have caught wind of this bug have taken measures already

It hasn't been patched yet but you can mitigate exposure of your systems.
Better yet, do what is written on tweakers.net

Quotes:

Make your store read-only or take it offline

If you can afford to take a PHP server offline for a day, do so. PHP core developer Gina Peter Banyard calls that the most sensible option. Several Dutch sites went offline as a precaution on October 21: tech site Tweakers, the House of Representatives (Tweede Kamer), the National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC) and security news site Security.NL.

Stop PHP-FPM and have your web server show a static maintenance page. The maintenance modes built into Magento and WordPress do not help: PHP still parses each request before the application checks for the maintenance flag.

If you cannot go offline, make the store read-only. Have your web server reject every request method other than GET and HEAD, for example in nginx:

if ($request_method !~ ^(GET|HEAD)$) {
return 503;
}

Quote:

Websites overnemen

De twee kritieke kwetsbaarheden in PHP (CVE-2026-109618 en CVE-2026-109619) hebben een score van 9,2 op de CVSS v4.0-schaal, die tot 10 gaat. Dat hoge cijfer is gebaseerd op de ernst van een kwetsbaarheid en op hoe makkelijk aanvallers die kunnen misbruiken. De kwetsbaarheden zouden al sinds versie 5.4.0 in PHP zitten, die in maart 2012 uitkwam. Aanvallers kunnen door de kwetsbaarheden eigen webpagina's publiceren. • FreeScout jsme vypnuli

@pulsar Thanks!

TL;DR: Details of two critical holes in PHP leaked before a fix was ready. They’re in how PHP handles file uploads and could let attackers run their own code on your server. Possibly affects PHP 5 through 8. Fixes are due today at 14:00 UTC, and attacks are expected within minutes of release.

https://www.vincentschmalbach.com/cve-2026-109618-and-cve-2026-109619-what-you-should-do-now/

The bug sits below WordPress or Laravel, so having no upload form doesn’t protect you, and nor do security plugins or maintenance mode.

Until the patch: list every server running PHP, including old staging sites. Switch off PHP’s upload-progress setting, and get your web server to refuse upload-style requests before they reach PHP. That breaks uploads for a few hours, which is the trade-off.

Once the fix lands: update every PHP version on every server, restart PHP and any background workers, and rebuild Docker images. PHP 8.1 and older won’t get a fix, so upgrade or take them offline. On managed hosting, ask your host to confirm.

CVE-2026-109618.description: PHP uses longjmp() for out-of-memory (OOM) errors to exit the current context and abort handling of the request. Some contexts may not properly account for this scenario and leave request memory in an uninitialized state before performing an allocation. The subsequent request cleanup procedure may read or branch on this memory. Multiple OOM strategies can consistently trigger this condition and lead to remote code execution (RCE).

Wise system administrators who have caught wind of this bug have taken measures already

It hasn't been patched yet but you can mitigate exposure of your systems.
Better yet, do what is written on tweakers.net

Quotes:

Make your store read-only or take it offline

If you can afford to take a PHP server offline for a day, do so. PHP core developer Gina Peter Banyard calls that the most sensible option. Several Dutch sites went offline as a precaution on October 21: tech site Tweakers, the House of Representatives (Tweede Kamer), the National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC) and security news site Security.NL.

Stop PHP-FPM and have your web server show a static maintenance page. The maintenance modes built into Magento and WordPress do not help: PHP still parses each request before the application checks for the maintenance flag.

If you cannot go offline, make the store read-only. Have your web server reject every request method other than GET and HEAD, for example in nginx:

if ($request_method !~ ^(GET|HEAD)$) {
return 503;
}

De twee kritieke kwetsbaarheden in PHP (CVE-2026-109618 en CVE-2026-109619) hebben een score van 9,2 op de CVSS v4.0-schaal, die tot 10 gaat. Dat hoge cijfer is gebaseerd op de ernst van een kwetsbaarheid en op hoe makkelijk aanvallers die kunnen misbruiken. De kwetsbaarheden zouden al sinds versie 5.4.0 in PHP zitten, die in maart 2012 uitkwam. Aanvallers kunnen door de kwetsbaarheden eigen webpagina's publiceren. • FreeScout jsme vypnuli

TL;DR: Details of two critical holes in PHP leaked before a fix was ready. They’re in how PHP handles file uploads and could let attackers run their own code on your server. Possibly affects PHP 5 through 8. Fixes are due today at 14:00 UTC, and attacks are expected within minutes of release.

https://www.vincentschmalbach.com/cve-2026-109618-and-cve-2026-109619-what-you-should-do-now/

The bug sits below WordPress or Laravel, so having no upload form doesn’t protect you, and nor do security plugins or maintenance mode.

Until the patch: list every server running PHP, including old staging sites. Switch off PHP’s upload-progress setting, and get your web server to refuse upload-style requests before they reach PHP. That breaks uploads for a few hours, which is the trade-off.

Once the fix lands: update every PHP version on every server, restart PHP and any background workers, and rebuild Docker images. PHP 8.1 and older won’t get a fix, so upgrade or take them offline. On managed hosting, ask your host to confirm.

CVE-2026-109619.description: PHP has various global state that temporarily points into request memory. In some scenarios, global state may not be correctly reset, or may be repopulated after being reset. The global state may then refer to request memory even after it has been freed. Subsequent requests may read or branch on this stale state before it is fully initialized. Multiple strategies can trigger this condition and produce remote code execution (RCE).

CVE-2026-109125.description: In NLnet Labs Unbound up to and including version 1.26.1, an observable  cache-level side-channel can be exposed with 'unwanted-reply-threshold > 0' configurations (not a default configuration). If a response-like UDP datagram reaches the upstream source port currently used by a recursive query, but its TXID does not match any pending query, Unbound counts the packet as an unwanted reply. When the accumulated count reaches the configured threshold, Unbound clears the worker's RRset cache and message cache. This cache clear action does not destroy the current upstream UDP pending query. Therefore, an external observer can distinguish whether a candidate port matches the current upstream source port by checking whether an existing cached item has been cleared. This is a cache side-channel vulnerability that can be used to probe the upstream source port. Although the attack is not feasible on default configurations and the suggested value (10 million) makes it an ureliable attack on a public resolver, in scenarios where the attacker can keep a concurrent query window alive, the attacker can first filter the source port and then perform birthday-style guessing against the TXID, making cache poisoning a feasible attack path.

CVE-2026-96405.description: NLnet Labs Unbound up to and including version 1.26.1 limits compression-pointer traversal for each individual domain-name operation but has no aggregate inbound decompression-work budget. Many chained compression pointers in a message results in a lot of CPU usage following them. A malicious actor with recursive-query access and control of an ordinarily delegated authority that serves specially crafted replies can exploit the vulnerability and degrade Unbound's general performance.
